title: Ninety Minutes
subtitle: Flash Flood, Evacuation & Campus Shelter

brief.userPrompt: A Thursday in late March 2027, run in the Week 11 lab of EMGT 4320 with student teams in the six seats. At 05:30 the NWS Charleston forecast office has a flash flood watch in effect for Athens County after 2 inches of rain overnight with 2 to 3 more inches forecast by noon; the Mill Street gauge on Sugar Camp Run reads 4.2 ft and rising (action stage 5.0, flood stage 7.0). Director of Emergency Management Renata Voss is the incident commander seat; the EOC is the Campus Services Building room 108. Timeline: 06:10 the gauge reads 5.0, Level 2; 06:40 an NWS flash flood warning for the Sugar Camp Run basin is issued, and the stage reaches 6.5 so Campus Police must close the Dairy Lane crossing (it floods at 8.0, and the central plant's fuel delivery truck is due at 08:00); 07:15 the stage is 7.0 and the Sugar Run Apartments (210 residents, 45 minute clearance) go on advisory; the Ohio River Forecast Center forecast crest is 10.8 ft at about 10:30, so the Riverside Hall (680 residents, 90 minute clearance, elevators lost when power is isolated) evacuation must be ordered by about 08:00 to be empty 30 minutes before the basement floods at 10.5; Facilities must move the truck fleet out of Lot C before 8.5 and library network gear and Special Collections boxes before 10.5 (2 and 3 hours); Kessler Fieldhouse takes 25 minutes to open by day and 40 at night (1,800 capacity, generator 36 hours), the Student Union ballroom (400) is the alternate once the count reaches 1,500; at 07:50 a viral post says Riverside Hall is already under water and trapped students are on the roof, a false rumor the PIO must check with Campus Police and correct on the same channel; a reporter from Channel 9 and the student newspaper The Hilltop call for a statement; parents call the 555-0150 line; two students with oxygen concentrators and a deaf student need support in the shelter; a student is not on any list at 09:30 and a parent says they are in Riverside Hall; the Clery Compliance Officer Hannah Fitch must classify the alerts as emergency notifications; the Red Cross chapter is asked to take over management after 12 hours; the Marlowe building inspector must clear Riverside Hall before reoccupation. The exercise runs in two phases for class time (05:30 to 09:30 and 09:30 to 13:00 exercise time) with a time jump. Evaluators and instructors score decisions against the role rubrics, not the outcome, and the exercise is no-fault. Do not name or invent any real student, record or accommodation.

Alerts follow the MSU Alert templates (160-character texts, what, where, what to do, next update) and the Clery emergency notification wording; NWS products follow the real format and are marked as exercise products; times are Eastern Daylight Time.

Player roles are only those in the audience list; NWS Charleston, the Ohio River Forecast Center, Marlowe Police and Fire, the Ohio Emergency Management Agency, the Red Cross, reporters, parents and residents are played by the SimCell. overview.theme: Deciding ahead of the trigger, one consistent public message against a fast-moving rumor, and caring for evacuated students, including students with access and functional needs, without losing count of anyone.
overview.threat: Before STARTEX, 2 inches of rain fell overnight on the 9-square-mile Sugar Camp Run basin north of campus. At 05:30 EDT on a Thursday in late March 2027, NWS Charleston has a flash flood watch in effect for Athens County, with 2 to 3 more inches forecast by noon. The Mill Street gauge reads 4.2 ft and is rising toward action stage (5.0) and flood stage (7.0). The creek can rise 1.5 feet per hour. By 06:40 an NWS flash flood warning covers the basin. The Ohio River Forecast Center then forecasts a crest of 10.8 ft at about 10:30. At that stage water reaches the Dairy Lane crossing, the Sugar Run Apartments, Parking Lot C and the Lower Quad, then floods the Riverside Hall basement (mechanical room, transformer vault, main electrical gear). Whitcomb Library's lower level floods only if the creek reaches 12.0, which stays a threat in play rather than the forecast.
overview.operationalImpact: Campus Police must close the Dairy Lane crossing at 6.5. That closure strands the central plant's 08:00 fuel delivery truck and cuts one Marlowe Fire access route. The 210 Sugar Run Apartments residents go on advisory at 7.0 with a 45-minute clearance. The Riverside Hall order for 680 residents across 11 floors has to go out by about 08:00. The hall needs 90 minutes to clear, longer once power isolation stops the elevators, and must be empty 30 minutes before the basement floods. Kessler Fieldhouse needs 25 minutes to open by day. It holds 1,800 and has 36 hours of generator power, and the Student Union ballroom (400) becomes the alternate once the count reaches 1,500. Shelter staff must support two students who use oxygen concentrators and a deaf student in the general population shelter. Facilities technicians race the stage to move the truck fleet and mobile generators out of Lot C before 8.5 and the library network gear and low-shelf Special Collections boxes to the second floor before 10.5. At 07:50 a viral post claims Riverside Hall is under water and students are trapped on the roof. Channel 9 and The Hilltop call for statements and the parent line fills with calls. At 09:30 a student is on no list while a parent insists the student is in Riverside Hall. After the time jump, the seats must plan the Red Cross handover and get the Marlowe building inspector to clear Riverside Hall before anyone moves back in. The exercise is no-fault. Evaluators score each decision against the role rubrics, not how the flood turns out.

overview.targetAudience: Student teams in six seats: Incident Commander (Emergency Manager), Public Information Officer (Director of University Communications), Chief of Campus Police, Dean of Students (Housing and Mass Care), Associate Vice President for Facilities, and Student Evaluators
overview.location: Marlowe State University (MSU) campus along Sugar Camp Run, with the EOC in Campus Services Building room 108; Marlowe, Athens County, Ohio

objectives.name: Decision Making
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to raise the EOC activation level and issue the Riverside Hall evacuation order by about 08:00, on the latest Ohio River Forecast Center crest forecast (10.8 ft at about 10:30) rather than waiting for the Mill Street gauge to reach the trigger, and to record the time and the forecast issuance behind each decision as EOP 4 requires.

objectives.name: Communication
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to send a first MSU Alert within 15 minutes of the flash flood warning, and to answer the 07:50 viral 'students trapped on the roof' post with one confirmed correction, checked with Campus Police and Facilities, on the same channel and consistent with the statements given to Channel 9, The Hilltop and the parent line.

objectives.name: Mass Care
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to open Kessler Fieldhouse as a general population shelter, support the two students who use oxygen concentrators and the deaf student in place, keep a shelter count that matches the Riverside Hall roster, and resolve the 09:30 missing-student report within the FERPA limits in MENSO 6.

objectives.name: Infrastructure Protection
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to tie the Dairy Lane closure, the Lot C fleet and generator move, the Riverside Hall power isolation and the Whitcomb Library equipment relocation to stage thresholds and clearance times, and to re-route the stranded central plant fuel delivery.

roles.name: Director of Emergency Management (Incident Commander)
roles.description: Owns the campus flood response, the EOC in Campus Services Building room 108, the activation level and the orders to close campus areas and evacuate residence halls.
standingOrders: Forecast, Not Gauge: decide on the latest forecast crest and clearance time; a 90-minute evacuation cannot wait for the gauge to reach 8.0.
Log It: record the time, the forecast issuance and the reason for every change of level and every order.
Consult, Then Act: consult the Vice President for Student Affairs when time allows, but do not let a phone call push the Riverside Hall order past its deadline.
One Picture: bring in the Marlowe Police and Fire liaisons at Level 1 and keep the Ohio EMA informed instead of running the response alone.

roles.name: Director of University Communications (Public Information Officer)
roles.description: Owns MSU Alert content, the website banner, social media, media statements and parent messages as the only university spokesperson.
standingOrders: Speed With a Holding Line: put out a first message fast and say when the next update will come; silence feeds rumors.
Verify Before You Deny: check every rumor with Campus Police or Facilities before answering it, and send the correction on the channel where the rumor spread.
Truth Over Reassurance: say what is known, what is not known and what is being done; never promise that a student is safe without confirmation.
One Voice: give Channel 9, the Marlowe Daily Ledger and The Hilltop the same statement and check it against the alert and the police message.

roles.name: Chief of Campus Police
roles.description: Owns road and crossing closures, access control, the Riverside Hall sweep, coordination with Marlowe Police and Fire, and notification decisions with the Clery Compliance Officer.
standingOrders: Close Early: close the Dairy Lane crossing at 6.5 ft, before it floods at 8.0, even if that strands the fuel truck and a fire access route.
Field Over Feed: if a social post and an officer on scene disagree, trust the officer and report back to the PIO.
Right Message Type: decide with the Clery Compliance Officer whether this is an emergency notification or a timely warning before the wording goes out.
Coordinate Access: tell Marlowe Fire about the lost route and agree on an alternate before you need it.

roles.name: Dean of Students (Housing and Mass Care)
roles.team: Team D: Housing and Mass Care
roles.description: Owns residence halls, the Kessler Fieldhouse shelter, student welfare, students with access and functional needs, and communication with parents about students.
standingOrders: Count Everyone: reconcile the Riverside Hall roster, the RA sweep and shelter registration; missing data is not a confirmed absence.

Support in Place: keep students with access and functional needs in the general population shelter with power for oxygen concentrators and communication access; never move them because of a disability.
FERPA Before Comfort: confirm to a parent that a student is accounted for only with consent or under the health and safety exception, decided with University Counsel.
Plan the Overflow: open the Student Union ballroom before Kessler reaches 1,500, not when it is full.

roles.name: Associate Vice President for Facilities
roles.description: Owns the central plant, electrical systems, building automation, flood barriers, pumps, the Mill Street gauge dashboard and damage assessment.
standingOrders: Move by Stage: get the fleet and the mobile generators out of Lot C before 8.5 ft and the library gear to the second floor before 10.5 ft; the clock is the stage, not the hour.
People Before Plant: isolate Riverside Hall power only after the IC confirms the elevators are clear of evacuating students.
Fuel the Shelter: secure generator fuel for Kessler's 36 hours and re-route the stranded plant delivery around Dairy Lane.
Gauge Honesty: report a gauge failure or a gap as missing data, never as a steady or falling stage.

roles.name: Student Evaluator
roles.description: Owns the observation record, timing each seat's decisions and scoring them against the role rubrics from the control table.
standingOrders: No Fault: score the decision and its basis, not how the flood turns out.
Timestamp Everything: record the exercise time of the trigger, the first public message and each order so timeliness criteria can be scored.
Evidence, Not Opinion: tie each score to a quoted action or message and the rubric level it meets.
Stay Silent: do not coach the seats or answer their questions during play.

phases.title: The Watch
phases.goal: Tests whether the seats act early on an uncertain forecast: they move from Level 3 Monitoring to Level 2 Partial and pre-position people and equipment before the Mill Street gauge forces them to.
beats: (05:30) SimCell as NWS Charleston delivers the exercise flash flood watch for Athens County: 2 inches fell overnight on the Sugar Camp Run basin and 2 to 3 more are forecast by noon. The Facilities dashboard shows the Mill Street gauge at 4.2 ft and rising. That puts the campus at Level 3 Monitoring under EOP 4. The IC decides whether to staff up now and logs the time and basis.

Noise item: the campus operations line reports a fire alarm trouble signal at a residence hall away from the floodplain, which turns out to be routine. Separately, someone asks whether this semester's MSU Alert system test has been recorded yet (MENSO 3).

(~06:00) The Mill Street gauge passes 5.0 ft, which is action stage and the Level 2 trigger. The IC opens the EOC in Campus Services Building room 108, with Police, Communications, Facilities and Student Affairs reporting. Facilities stages sandbags and pumps, and the Dean of Students alerts Riverside Hall and Sugar Run Apartments RAs and the Kessler Fieldhouse shelter team.

First schedule question: the central plant asks whether to call off or re-route the 08:00 fuel truck, which uses the Dairy Lane crossing. Residence Life asks whether 08:00 classes and Riverside Hall laundry and mechanical room access should continue. Facilities asks whether to start moving the fleet and mobile generators out of Parking Lot C now.

phases.title: Warning and Rising Water
phases.goal: Tests speed and accuracy of the first public warning and the stage-tied infrastructure actions as the flash flood warning arrives and the creek climbs toward flood stage.
beats: (06:40) SimCell delivers the exercise NWS flash flood warning for the Sugar Camp Run basin (CONSIDERABLE tag). The PIO's clock starts: the first MSU Alert must go out by 06:55 using the 160-character template (what, where, what to do, next update). The Clery Compliance Officer is consulted on whether it is an emergency notification under MENSO 3.

Time jump: the gauge passes 6.5 ft (~07:00) and Campus Police close the Dairy Lane crossing. Two consequences follow: the central plant's 08:00 fuel truck is stranded, and Marlowe Police and Fire (SimCell) lose one access route and ask which alternate route MSU recommends. Facilities must re-route or reschedule the fuel delivery.
Red herring: a custodian calls in 'water in the Riverside Hall basement.' A Facilities check finds a backed-up floor drain in the laundry room, not floodwater. Seats must verify before acting on it.

(~07:20) The gauge passes 7.0 ft, which is flood stage and the Level 1 trigger. Sugar Run Apartments go on evacuation advisory with a 45-minute clearance. A field photo of Sugar Camp Run at the top of its Upper Quad channel is shown on the projector, along with the dashboard reading.

SimCell as the Ohio River Forecast Center issues a forecast crest of 10.8 ft at about 10:30. That is above the 10.5 ft at which the Riverside Hall basement floods (mechanical room, transformer vault, main electrical gear). The seats must name this forecast issuance in any decision log entry they make from here on.

phases.title: The Riverside Decision
phases.goal: Tests the one decision point: ordering the evacuation of Riverside Hall's 680 residents by about 08:00 on the forecast crest rather than waiting for the gauge, opening Kessler Fieldhouse, and holding one consistent message against a viral rumor.
beats: DECISION POINT (07:30–08:00): The IC must decide whether to order the Riverside Hall evacuation now, on the 10.8 ft crest forecast, or wait for the EOP 2 trigger of 8.0 ft plus a forecast of 10.5 ft within 3 hours. Ordering now means 680 students across 11 floors move before dawn classes, on a forecast that could fall. Waiting risks the hall not clearing in its 90 minutes, longer once power isolation stops the elevators, and not being empty 30 minutes before the basement floods. The IC logs the time, the forecast issuance and the consultation with the Vice President for Student Affairs.

Once the order is given, the PIO must issue the first public message within 15 minutes (EOP 6) through MSU Alert, sirens, the website banner, the RA phone tree and door-to-door checks by Campus Police and Residence Life. Under MENSO 3 the PIO does not wait for Clery confirmation. The Dean of Students opens Kessler Fieldhouse, which takes 25 minutes, holds 1,800 and has 36 hours of generator power. The Student Union ballroom becomes the alternate once the count reaches 1,500.

Access and functional needs: two residents who use oxygen concentrators and one deaf resident need support in place at Kessler Fieldhouse. The shelter must plan generator-backed power outlets and communication access, and must not refer these students elsewhere. Facilities sequences the Riverside Hall power isolation against the elevator time the evacuation still needs.

(07:50) A viral post claims Riverside Hall is under water and students are trapped on the roof. Channel 9 and The Hilltop (SimCell) call with deadlines, and the parent line fills with calls. The PIO must publish one correction, confirmed with Campus Police and Facilities, on the same channel as the post. It must match what reporters and parents are told (MENSO 6).

Stage race: the gauge passes 8.0 ft and floods the Dairy Lane crossing. Facilities must get the truck fleet and mobile generators out of Parking Lot C before 8.5 ft (the lot floods at 9.5). Library staff ask when to start moving Whitcomb Library network gear and low-shelf Special Collections boxes to the second floor ahead of 10.5 ft.

phases.title: Crest and Return
phases.goal: Tests accountability for every resident through the crest, then recovery planning: the Red Cross handover, damage reporting and a reoccupation that is cleared by inspection rather than by the clock.
beats: (09:30) A parent (SimCell) insists their student lives in Riverside Hall, but the student is on neither the Kessler Fieldhouse registration nor the hall roster. The Dean of Students and Campus Police must reconcile the shelter count with the Riverside Hall roster and with the Ohio EMA flood damage report. The PIO must answer the parent within the FERPA limits in MENSO 6. No student is named in the inject.

(10:30) The gauge crests near 10.8 ft and floods the Riverside Hall basement, Lot C and the Lower Quad. An exercise ORFC update says a renewed rain band could carry the creek to 12.0 ft, which would flood Whitcomb Library's lower level. Facilities confirms what was moved upstairs and what is still at risk.

Hurdle: the central plant's fuel delivery still cannot get through while Dairy Lane stays closed. Kessler Fieldhouse is on generator, the shelter count is close to 1,500, and the Dean must decide when to open the Student Union ballroom as the alternate shelter.

Time jump to the recovery period. Under EOP 10, Facilities lays out the building-by-building inspection: structure, electrical, water, mechanical, fire alarm, elevator. Riverside Hall stays closed until the Marlowe building inspector gives written clearance. The IC records damage figures for the Ohio Emergency Management Agency (SimCell).

The seats plan the Red Cross handover of shelter operations and temporary housing for displaced Riverside Hall residents. The PIO issues a reoccupation and class-schedule message, and the IC lowers the activation level with the time and basis recorded. ENDEX.

DoS also sets the Student Union ballroom trigger at 1,500 and staffs registration from the first arrival. Fac sends fuel to the Kessler day tank, using the re-routed tanker if it can get in. Fac tells the electrician to hold the breaker until the IC confirms the elevators are clear of evacuating students (EOP Annex F sections 5 and 7).

Radio Call (Riverside Hall Director, 08:25): "EOC, Riverside. My RAs started knocking on their floors at 07:50 on their own, because residents were already in the halls, whether or not anyone has told me to go. Floors 1 through 5 report clear. 6 through 11 are still knocking, and the stair tower is slow. Both oxygen residents are on 9 with the nurse, waiting for the elevator. One RA can't tell me whether anyone has knocked for our deaf resident. My roster says 680. The RA floor sheets add up to 412 out so far, and I can't match names to the sheets. Some residents are walking to 08:00 classes across the Lower Quad, and the paths are awash. I need two answers from you right now. Is this an evacuation order with Kessler as the destination? And who tells me when to give up the elevator?"
Radio Call (Facilities electrician at the Riverside transformer vault, 08:27): "Ops, there's water seeping into the vault sump. I can hold the main breaker closed until about 09:15, no later. After that I'm pulling it whether the elevators are empty or not, or I'm getting out of here."
Shelter Status (Kessler registration desk, 08:25): "Kessler Fieldhouse OPEN. Registered: 318. Cots set: 600. Generator outlets: LOW (2 reserved for oxygen). Water: OK."
Control-table note to Student Evaluators (from the TA): "Record the exercise time of any Riverside order, of the first MSU Alert, and of the correction to the roof rumor. Record when Fac opens the Riverside main breaker and what confirmation, if any, the seats exchange before it is opened. Copy log entries exactly as the seats write them. Do not prompt."
msel.expectedAction: If the IC has not yet ordered the Riverside evacuation, the IC orders it now. If the order is already out, the IC confirms it and names the area, the clearance time and Kessler as the shelter (MENSO 5). The IC logs the time and the 0720 AM crest forecast as the basis, and reroutes residents off the Lower Quad paths (EOP Annex F 5.3 and 5.5). The Dean of Students puts an officer or RA on the door of the deaf resident and holds one elevator for floor 9 until both oxygen residents are out. The Dean also starts reconciling the roster, the RA floor sheets and Kessler registration, treating unmatched names as unaccounted for, not as absent. Fac holds the main breaker until the IC confirms the elevators are clear, and plans the isolation before the electrician's 09:15 limit (EOP Annex F 5.6). Evaluators timestamp each step.

msel.event:
Scenario time 09:45. Radio Call (Campus Police sergeant, Riverside lobby): "Chief, Sergeant on Riverside. We finished the final floor-by-floor sweep with a Marlowe Fire crew. Doors knocked and master-keyed on all 11 floors. We found two residents on floor 10: one asleep with headphones in, one who came back for a laptop. Both are walking to Kessler with an officer now. Both elevator cars are at the lobby, empty and locked out. Nobody's on the roof. The roof hatch is padlocked from the inside and nobody has touched it. I'm the last one out unless you tell me otherwise."
Radio Call (Riverside Hall Director, 09:47): "EOC, Riverside. Here's the update on the 15 not on any list. The 2 from the sweep are now accounted for. 6 more replied to their RA's group text saying they slept off campus last night, but we have no face-to-face confirmation for them. 7 are still unconfirmed, and one of them is on the fourth floor. The sweep found nobody on four. The 3 walk-ins at Kessler who say they live in Riverside still aren't on my roster."
Radio Call (Facilities electrician at the transformer vault, 09:48): "Ops, the stage is 10.3 and water is seeping under the vault door. I need the go to open the main breaker in the next ten minutes or I'm pulling out of here myself."

The IC then authorizes Fac to isolate Riverside power before the basement stage (EOP Annex F 5.6, People Before Plant). DoS keeps the 7 as unconfirmed, not absent, keeps contacting them and checks the 3 walk-ins with Housing. Any answer to the fourth-floor parent goes through the FERPA consent or health-and-safety exception decided with University Counsel. CPD passes the 'no one on the roof' field report to the PIO for the rumor correction. (If no order was given earlier, the Hall Director began the sweep on his own at 08:00 when water reached the lobby; the facilitator reads the sweep report either way.)

hotwash.methodDescription: Ask the room for three things that went well and three things that broke or failed during the flood response. Go around the room one team at a time (EOC command, Facilities, Police, Communications, Student Affairs/shelter), write each item on the whiteboard in two columns, and don't let anyone repeat an item until every team has spoken.

questions.text: At 07:35 (I-12) the Vice President for Student Affairs asked you to hold the Riverside evacuation until the Mill Street gauge actually reached 8.0 and the 9 AM forecast came out. The Hall Director had just told you a full sweep takes about 90 minutes, and longer for floors 9 to 11 and the three residents on the access list. Did you decide on the 10.8 ft crest forecast, or did you wait for the gauge? What time did you give the order, and which forecast issuance did you write down as the basis, as EOP 4 requires? What would have let you decide faster?

At 06:10 (I-04) the gauge passed action stage at 5.02 ft and was rising 1.2 ft/hr. Then the central plant needed an answer about the 08:00 diesel tanker by 06:45, and the fleet coordinator asked whether to start the 40-minute Lot C move now or wait for 8.5 (I-05). Did you work back from the 6.5 Dairy Lane closure and the 9.5 Lot C stage to a start time, or did you wait for each threshold to arrive? When Tech 4 reported two inches in the low corner of Lot C at 07:20, were the trucks and generators already moving? Did the tanker reach Kessler's half-full day tank?

At 07:50 (I-13) the 'trapped on the roof' post had 900 reposts in 8 minutes. Channel 9 was going live at 8:00, The Hilltop was publishing at 08:15, and 64 voicemails were waiting on the parent line. What had you already told the public when the flash flood warning came out, and was it within 15 minutes? Who checked the roof claim with Campus Police and Facilities before you answered? Was your correction one message, on the same channel, saying the same thing to Channel 9, The Hilltop and parents, or did different versions go out?

When Riverside emptied into Kessler Fieldhouse, how did you keep the shelter count tied to the 680-resident roster? How did you support the two students on oxygen concentrators and the deaf student, both during the evacuation and at the shelter? When the missing-student report came in at 09:30, what were you able to confirm, and to whom, within the FERPA limits in MENSO 6? Where did the shelter team depend on the residence hall staff or the police for information, and what was missing?

At 10:32 (I-18) the gauge read 10.81 ft with a 'CREST?' flag, and the 10:15 forecast said the crest was over but a second rise toward 12.0 ft was possible late in the afternoon. Did operations and the technical team read that forecast the same way? Did the 48 boxes still on the lower level and the floor-level UPS and switches in Whitcomb get moved, or did 'not in this forecast' lead you to stand down? When did you bring in the Marlowe and Athens County emergency management liaisons and NWS Charleston, and was that early enough?

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: NWS Charleston WV forecast office duty forecaster and the Ohio River Forecast Center hydrologist (weather and hazard authority)
simcellScripts.trigger: IC, Facilities or PIO calls the NWS Charleston office or the Ohio River Forecast Center to confirm the watch or warning, ask how sure the crest forecast is, or report the Mill Street gauge readings
hardQuestions: What's your gauge reading right now, and what time was it taken? I need a number and a time, not 'it's high.' If your dashboard has gone flat, tell me. Missing data isn't zero.
Which issuance are you working from? The 0540 AM crest was 2.3 feet lower and 3 hours later. If your plan is built on that one, it's out of date.

You're asking if 10.8 is a sure thing. No forecast is. The 0720 includes 1.5 to 2 inches of QPF through 10 AM. Do you have a decision you can make on that, or are you waiting for one I can't give you?
Are you seeing debris racking on the Mill Street culvert? That can push your local stage above anything in my forecast. Have you got anyone watching it?
concessions: When Facilities gives timed gauge readings and the debris report, the forecaster logs them as a ground truth report and confirms the 0720 AM issuance is the current forecast. The next issuance is due by 09:00 or sooner.

When the IC explains the Riverside 10.5 ft impact, the hydrologist confirms the forecast puts 10.5 ft near 10 AM. They will not say whether to evacuate: 'That's your call, and you've got the numbers to make it.'
After 10:15, if asked, they say the second rain band might bring a rise to near 12.0 ft. They call it possible and say it is not in the forecast.

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: Ohio Emergency Management Agency watch desk (with Athens County EMA duty officer on the same bridge line)
simcellScripts.trigger: IC or Housing and Mass Care calls county or state emergency management to report the activation, ask for resources (fuel, interpreter, cots), or answer the 09:32 and 15:40 data requests
hardQuestions: What's your activation level, and since when? I need a time and a reason for the log.
How many people are displaced right now, from Riverside and from the Sugar Run Apartments? How many are actually in Kessler? Don't give me 680 if 61 signed out to friends.
You want a fuel delivery for the Kessler generator. What's your tank level, your burn rate and your hours remaining? And which road can a tanker actually use, with Dairy Lane under water?
Your 11:00 numbers are late. Do you have a single point of contact for the county, or am I calling four people?
concessions: Once the shelter count is reconciled (start + arrivals − departures) and broken out by Riverside and Sugar Run Apartments, the desk takes it as the preliminary displaced figure and stops calling for it.

Once Facilities gives the generator fuel level, burn rate and a usable access route, the county logs a fuel resource request and gives an ETA window. It will not arrive before the crossing reopens unless MSU names another route.
Once the IC names one point of contact per shift, all county and state requests go through that person.

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: Marlowe Fire dispatcher (also relays for Marlowe Police)
simcellScripts.trigger: Campus Police announces or considers the Dairy Lane closure, asks for help with the Riverside sweep, or Marlowe Fire calls in at I-09
hardQuestions: Dairy Lane is our first-due route to your south side. Which route do you want Engine 2 and the medic units on, and does it still work at 9.0 when your Lower Quad goes under?
Is there an officer at the barricade, or just cones? People drive around cones. We've pulled them out of the water before.
You're asking for a crew on the Riverside sweep. How many floors are left, how many people are unaccounted for, and who's my one contact in your EOC?
Is anyone actually on the Riverside roof? I've got a viral post and two citizen calls. Confirm it or rule it out. I'm not sending a ladder truck on a rumor.
concessions: Once Campus Police names the alternate route and a staffed barricade, dispatch updates its run cards and confirms Engine 2 has the route.
Once the Chief names a single point of contact and shares the evacuation area and the list of unaccounted residents, Marlowe Fire sends one crew to join the floor-by-floor sweep.
Once the sweep reports the roof hatch padlocked from inside and no one on the roof, Marlowe Fire tells its own public line 'no roof rescue in progress.' It refers questions to MSU.

hardQuestions: We go live at 8:00 with or without you. Is anyone on the Riverside roof, yes or no? I need a name and a title for the quote.

assumptions: The exercise is conducted in a no-fault learning environment. It tests the plans and the decisions made in this room, not the individual EMGT 4320 students who hold the seats.
The scenario is plausible, and events occur as they are presented. Gauge readings, forecasts and field reports are accurate when they are delivered, unless an inject itself is uncertain.

Players respond in accordance with existing plans, policies and procedures, mainly the MSU EOP Annex F and the Notification and Shelter SOP. Where the plans are silent, players state what they would do and why.
Decisions and orders made in one module stay in force in later modules. Anything not decided stays undecided, and the hazard keeps developing either way.
Players use only the information they have in the room at that moment. No one knows what later forecasts, gauge readings or field reports will show.
artificialities: The four modules cover about five hours of scenario time, and Phase 4 covers Thursday afternoon. The facilitator moves time forward with read-aloud time-jump cards, and from 08:30 the SimCell compresses time further, so each inject carries its own scenario time.

The SimCell at the control table plays everyone outside the room. That includes the NWS Charleston forecast office, the Ohio River Forecast Center, the Ohio Emergency Management Agency, Marlowe Police and Fire, the Vice President for Student Affairs, the Red Cross chapter, the Marlowe building inspector, the media, parents and field staff.

MSU Alert, the outdoor sirens, the Facilities dashboard, the parent line, the website banner and social media are named as in the plans but are not used. Players say or write the message they would send, and the time they would send it.
Injects arrive on paper, on the projector or as a phone or radio call from the SimCell. The Wireless Emergency Alert tones, gauge alarms, photos and posts are simulated.
Student Evaluators record times and quotes at the control table and do not take part in play. The EOC in Campus Services Building room 108 is represented by this room.

modules.narrativeMd:
**Module 3 — The Riverside Decision (exercise time 2:00–3:00, 07:30–08:30 EDT)**

It is 07:30 EDT. First light is over the Upper Quad, and the heaviest rain is falling on the basin. NWS Charleston issued a Flash Flood Warning at 06:40 for central Athens County, including the Sugar Camp Run basin and the campus, until 12:45 PM. Wireless Emergency Alert tones went off on phones across campus. The Clery Compliance Officer asked for a classification decision before any MSU Alert goes out. In the Parents & Families group, a parent reported that the parent line went to voicemail, and commenters claimed the creek was already in Riverside's basement. At 06:53, a custodian reported an inch of water on the Riverside basement floor near the laundry.

The gauge passed 6.5 ft at 07:02. Marlowe Fire asked for an alternate route for Engine 2 and the medic units. The diesel driver was already on the road over Dairy Lane. Flood stage, 7.0 ft, was passed at 07:20, and the low corner of Lot C is ponding. The 07:20 Ohio River Forecast Center issuance calls for 8.0 ft near 08:00, 9.5 ft near 09:00, 10.5 ft near 10:00 and a crest of 10.8 ft near 10:30. That crest is 2.3 ft higher and about 3 hours earlier than the previous forecast. The gauge now reads 7.31 ft and is rising about 1.7 ft per hour. Riverside's 680 residents are waking for 08:00 classes across the Lower Quad. The Riverside clearance clock is running whether or not anyone starts it.

Working backward from the 10.5 ft basement stage using the 90-minute clearance time and the 30-minute buffer
Opening Kessler Fieldhouse and supporting residents on oxygen concentrators and the deaf resident
Isolating power to Riverside without stopping elevators that are still in use
Correcting a viral rumor once, accurately, and the same way on every channel
Lot C and Whitcomb Library moves racing the rising water

**Module 4 — Crest and Return (exercise time 3:00–4:00, 08:30–09:30 EDT; scenario time compressed through Thursday evening)**

It is 08:30 EDT. In the last hour, the Vice President for Student Affairs asked the EOC to hold the Riverside evacuation until the gauge reached 8.0 ft. The Riverside Director reported about 90 minutes to clear 11 floors, plus three residents on the access list. Kessler could be open 25 minutes after a go, with a half-full generator day tank and few generator outlets. The Riverside electrician asked when to open the main breaker. At 07:50, an X post claiming students were trapped on the Riverside roof spread quickly. Channel 9 and The Hilltop asked for confirmation before their 08:00 and 08:15 deadlines, and voicemails piled up on the parent line.

The gauge passed 8.0 ft at 08:04, and the Dairy Lane crossing is under water. In Lot C, a generator trailer has a seized jack stand. Library staff asked whether to start moving boxes and network gear. A career fair in the Student Union is still planning to open at 09:00. At 08:25, Riverside reported floors 1 through 6 clear and floors 7 through 11 in progress. Both oxygen residents were on their way to Kessler with a nurse, and the deaf resident was out. The Riverside roster and the RA floor sheets do not match yet. Kessler was open with 318 registered. Since then the creek has spread onto the Lower Quad paths, and registration is climbing. From now on the SimCell compresses time, and each inject carries its own scenario time. The crest is expected near 10:30, followed by the recovery afternoon. Every order you have given stays in force.
